purpose: Rules for weapons/platforms that do not exist in historical combat data, exist at different dates, or materially diverge from the historical type sharing their name.
procedure: 1 Identify the actual branch designation/configuration and historical_relation before using historical performance assumptions.
2 Resolve engineering capability: speed/range/endurance/protection/sensors/weapons/reliability and relevant failure modes.
3 Resolve maturity separately: prototype, trial, production, commissioned, crew-workup, combat-ready.
4 Resolve quantity and allocation separately from existence. A design entry is never fleet strength.
5 Resolve mission fit and causal stages. A strong system can be irrelevant to an event if geometry, doctrine, supply or allocation prevents use.
6 Use historical analogues only as bounded component priors where mechanisms are shared. Never import the historical analogue combat record as the result.
7 Record enemy observation/adaptation only after the system has plausibly been encountered; do not grant prescient countermeasures.
8 If capability, provenance or maturity is missing for an event-local ahistorical/divergent system, keep combat resolution unready rather than assigning a neutral modifier.
anti_bias_examples: A 潜高 boat is not evaluated as an ordinary historical Japanese submarine merely because it carries torpedoes.
A branch-specific Zero engine variant is not evaluated from the historical Zero model name alone.
A future new weapon with no historical counterpart receives no automatic weakness and no automatic superiority; mechanism and maturity determine the band.
